title: A plugin's operations: plugins/<name>/core/operations.json
description: Everything a plugin can do for an agent or for another plugin, declared once: each operation's input and output as JSON Schema, the errors it can end with, whether its vault performs it (it needs a secret), and whether the model gets it as a tool. Other plugins name it <plugin>.<operation>. Text the model reads (what a tool does, what each argument is for, what an error means) lives in core/model.ftl, not here. Within a version, changes only add.

id.description: Lowercase words joined by -: the operation's id here, its message id in model.ftl, and the second half of <plugin>.<operation>.

input.description: A JSON Schema for an object: the operation's arguments, each a property. With a tool, model.ftl's message for the operation has one attribute per property, saying what it is for.

output.description: A JSON Schema for what the operation answers with.

errors.description: The errors the operation can end with, by id; model.ftl's message error-<id> says what each means.

vault.description: The plugin's vault performs it: it needs a secret, which never leaves the vault.

tool.description: The model gets the operation as a tool, described by model.ftl's message for the operation. The hints are MCP's tool annotations; alwaysLoad keeps the tool in front of tool search, and runsCode says it runs code the model wrote, which omp approves as code execution.
